name: Flying Pancakes
subject: pancakes
dek: The world’s pancakes and their griddled relatives.

items.name: Acadian ployes
items.flavor: Mild buckwheat, a little sour from the grain, with a holey top and a soft underside.

items.name: Adai
items.flavor: A sturdy mixed-lentil pancake, peppery and hot from dried chile, with curry leaf in the batter.

items.name: Aebleskiver
items.flavor: Round Danish pancakes from a molded pan, cardamom, jam, and powdered sugar.

items.name: Aegean akıtma
items.flavor: Thin Aegean semolina pancakes with a tangy crumb, finished with walnuts and syrup.

items.name: Afghan bolani
items.flavor: Crisp stuffed flatbread filled with seasoned potato and leek, mild with green chile.

items.name: Äggakaka
items.flavor: A thick Scanian egg pancake, served with fried pork and lingonberries.

items.name: Åland pancake
items.flavor: A baked porridge pancake from Åland, cardamom-scented, with prune jam.

items.name: Alaska sourdough flapjacks
items.flavor: Mildly sour wheat cakes, a little richer from evaporated milk, with a browned edge.

items.name: Algerian mahjouba
items.flavor: Thin semolina flatbread folded around a tomato, onion, and chile filling.

items.name: Aloo paratha
items.flavor: A wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato, griddled in ghee until the surface is spotted and flaky.

items.name: Amboli
items.flavor: A soft, spongy, lightly sour rice pancake from the Konkan coast.

items.name: Apam balik
items.flavor: A turnover pancake folded over crushed peanuts, sugar, and a little butter.

items.name: Appalachian buckwheat cakes
items.flavor: Earthly and slightly sour, with a gray-brown crumb and a sorghum finish if you use it at the table.

items.name: Appalachian dried-apple pancakes
items.flavor: Soft wheat cakes with chewy, tart pieces of dried apple and a hint of cinnamon.

items.name: Appalachian sorghum pancakes
items.flavor: Malty and lightly bitter-sweet from sorghum, with a plain wheat crumb underneath.

items.name: Appam
items.flavor: A bowl-shaped rice hopper with a lacy crisp rim, a spongy sweet center, and coconut in the batter.

items.name: Apple cider pancakes
items.flavor: Reduced sweet cider and soft apple pieces in a lightly spiced wheat cake.

items.name: Arepa boyacense
items.flavor: A lightly sweet highland cake of corn and wheat, studded with cuajada and cooked on a griddle.

items.name: Arepa de choclo
items.flavor: A thick sweet-corn cake with pockets of fresh cheese, griddled until the edges brown.

items.name: Arepa de huevo
items.flavor: A fried corn cake with a whole egg cooked inside, crisp outside and set in the middle.

items.name: Arepa santandereana
items.flavor: A thick yellow-corn cake, griddled, served with crisp pork chicharrón.

items.name: Argentine panqueques
items.flavor: Thin milk crepes rolled around dulce de leche, with a browned-butter edge.

items.name: Australian pancakes
items.flavor: Wide, thin lemon-and-sugar pancakes with a lacy brown rim and a soft center.

items.name: Australian pikelets
items.flavor: Small, thick drop pancakes with a soft crumb, eaten with butter and jam at tea.

items.name: Azerbaijani qutab
items.flavor: Thin half-moon flatbread stuffed with herbs, finished with sumac.

items.name: Bacon griddle cakes
items.flavor: Salty, smoky bacon in a lightly sweet wheat pancake, cooked in bacon fat.

items.name: Bahamian johnnycake
items.flavor: A mildly sweet wheat cake, buttery, cooked covered in a skillet so the center steams.

items.name: Bananas Foster pancakes
items.flavor: A plain buttermilk pancake under bananas in brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, and rum.

items.name: Banh khot
items.flavor: Tiny crisp-edged rice cakes from a dimpled pan, each topped with a shrimp and a soft coconut center.

items.name: Banh xeo
items.flavor: A turmeric-yellow rice crepe, crisp at the edge, filled with pork, shrimp, and bean sprouts.

items.name: Basque talo
items.flavor: A griddled corn flatbread from the Basque Country, often wrapped around sausage or eaten with cider.

items.name: Belarusian draniki
items.flavor: Belarusian potato pancakes bound with potato starch and egg, sour cream on the side.

items.name: Besan cheela
items.flavor: A savory gram-flour pancake with onion, ajwain, and cumin, soft in the middle and spotted brown.

items.name: Bindaetteok
items.flavor: A coarse mung-bean pancake with pork, sour kimchi, and a toasted sesame edge.

items.name: Blinchiki
items.flavor: Thin Russian crepes rolled around a sweet farmer-cheese filling.

items.name: Bolivian buñuelos
items.flavor: Puffed fried dough scented with anise, served beside a cup of api, not cooked in it.

items.name: Brazilian beiju
items.flavor: A plain tapioca flatbread, soft or crisp depending on how long it stays on the griddle, with almost no seasoning.

items.name: Brazilian panquecas
items.flavor: Thin wheat crepes rolled around seasoned ground beef and a simple tomato sauce.

items.name: Brazilian tapioca crepes
items.flavor: A lacy crepe of hydrated tapioca starch, folded over fresh cheese, chewy and mild.

items.name: Breton crepes
items.flavor: Thin wheat crepes from Brittany, butter and sugar, the cake of Chandeleur.

items.name: Buchujeon
items.flavor: A garlic-chive pancake, green and savory, with a light wheat crust and no seafood.

items.name: Buckwheat blini
items.flavor: Yeasted buckwheat blini, earthier than the wheat cakes, for butter and sour cream.

items.name: Buckwheat galette
items.flavor: A savory Breton buckwheat crepe, lacy and a little bitter, cooked on a billig.

items.name: Bulgarian palachinki
items.flavor: Thin Bulgarian pancakes with yogurt in the batter, sweet or with white cheese.

items.name: Cachapas
items.flavor: Coarse sweet-corn pancakes folded over fresh white cheese, juicy rather than bready.

items.name: Cape Cod cranberry hotcakes
items.flavor: Tart cranberry pieces in a lightly sweet, orange-scented wheat cake.

items.name: Chatamari
items.flavor: A thin Newar rice crepe topped with egg, onion, and a little chile.

items.name: Cheese blintzes
items.flavor: A thin, lightly sweet pancake wrapped around tangy soft cheese and fried in butter.

items.name: Chilean panqueques
items.flavor: Thin wheat crepes filled with manjar and finished with a dry dust of powdered sugar.

items.name: Chilean sopaipillas
items.flavor: Fried pumpkin rounds, crisp and puffed, eaten with pebre or with chancaca syrup.

items.name: Chilote milcao
items.flavor: Pan-fried cakes of raw and cooked potato, salty, crisp at the edge, and dense inside.

items.name: Chitoi pitha
items.flavor: Small, soft rice cakes with a dimpled top, mild and a little sweet if date molasses is poured on.

items.name: Chocolate chip pancakes
items.flavor: A plain sweet pancake with pockets of melted semisweet chocolate.

items.name: Colombian arepas
items.flavor: A thinner white-corn arepa with cheese in the dough, buttered, beside tomato and scallion hogao.

items.name: Cong you bing
items.flavor: A flaky wheat cake layered with scallion and oil, crisp outside and chewy within.

items.name: Corn oysters
items.flavor: Sweet corn, egg, and pepper, fried in small irregular cakes.

items.name: Corn tortillas
items.flavor: Soft, toasted corn with a faint mineral note from nixtamal, cooked dry on a hot comal.

items.name: Costa Rican chorreadas
items.flavor: Sweet fresh-corn pancakes, lightly eggy, served with sour cream.

items.name: Crêpes Suzette
items.flavor: Thin crepes in orange butter, with a warm orange sauce.

items.name: Crespelle
items.flavor: Italian crepes, plain or baked. Crespelle alla fiorentina is one variation, not the only form.

items.name: Croatian palačinke
items.flavor: Croatian crepes rolled with fresh cheese, lemon, and raisins.

items.name: Cuban torrejas
items.flavor: Day-old bread soaked in egg and milk, fried, and finished with cinnamon syrup and a splash of wine.

items.name: Czech lívance
items.flavor: Small yeasted Czech pancakes served with quark and jam, not rolled.

items.name: Czech palačinky
items.flavor: Thin Czech crepes filled with sweet quark and raisins.

items.name: Dadar gulung
items.flavor: A green pandan crepe rolled around grated coconut and palm sugar.

items.name: Danish pandekager
items.flavor: Thin Danish pancakes, rolled with sugar or jam.

items.name: Derbyshire oatcakes
items.flavor: A yeasted oatmeal pancake from Derbyshire, a little thicker than the Staffordshire shop cake.

items.name: Deruny
items.flavor: Ukrainian grated-potato pancakes, fried crisp and served with sour cream.

items.name: Diner silver-dollar pancakes
items.flavor: Mild, buttery, and lightly sweet, with more browned edge than center because the cakes are small.

items.name: Djiboutian lahoh
items.flavor: Small, holey breakfast cakes, mildly sour, with a soft wheat crumb.

items.name: Dominican casabe
items.flavor: A thin, dry cassava flatbread, lightly salty, crisp at the edge and bland in a way that suits a stew.

items.name: Dominican yaniqueques
items.flavor: Small wheat rounds, salty and toasted, cooked in a slick of oil until both sides spot.

items.name: Dorayaki
items.flavor: Two small golden-brown pancakes sandwiched around sweet red bean paste.

items.name: Drie-in-de-pan
items.flavor: Three small Dutch pancakes in the pan, with apple in the batter.

items.name: Dutch baby
items.flavor: Eggy, custardy in the center, and crisp at the lifted rim, with browned butter.

items.name: Dutch pannenkoeken
items.flavor: Large, thin Dutch pancakes, plate-sized, with syrup, apple, or bacon.

items.name: Egg foo young
items.flavor: A thick egg pancake with bean sprouts and onion, covered in a brown gravy.

items.name: Egg hoppers
items.flavor: A coconut rice hopper with a soft egg set in the center, crisp at the rim.

items.name: Egyptian qatayef
items.flavor: Yeasted pancakes stuffed with cinnamon walnuts and soaked in a lemon-rose syrup.

items.name: Emirati chebab
items.flavor: Small yeasted pancakes perfumed with saffron and cardamom, served with date syrup.

items.name: English crumpets
items.flavor: Ring-cooked yeast cakes, toasted so butter sinks into the holes.

items.name: English pikelets
items.flavor: Small freeform yeast cakes with a holey top, toasted and buttered.

items.name: English Shrove pancakes
items.flavor: Thin egg pancakes, lemon and sugar, made to clear the kitchen before Lent.

items.name: Eritrean taita
items.flavor: Sour teff flatbread with a spongy top, meant to carry tsebhi.

items.name: Estonian kohupiim pancakes
items.flavor: Small fried cakes of Estonian kohupiim, a curd cheese, with jam.

items.name: Ethiopian kita
items.flavor: Mild, soft teff flatbread with a light toasted face and no sour ferment.

items.name: Farinata
items.flavor: Ligurian chickpea flatbread, baked thick enough to stay creamy, with oil and pepper.

items.name: Farmer cheese latkes
items.flavor: The older Ashkenazi Hanukkah pancake, made of farmer cheese rather than potato.

items.name: Ficelle picarde
items.flavor: A Picardy crepe rolled around ham and mushrooms in cream, then baked with cheese.

items.name: Fijian babakau
items.flavor: Soft yeasted dough, fried, with a mild sweetness and a pale, airy center.

items.name: Filipino hotcakes
items.flavor: Soft wheat breakfast pancakes, browned in margarine and eaten with sugar or condensed milk.

items.name: Filloas
items.flavor: Thin Galician Carnival pancakes, scented with anise, rolled with sugar.

items.name: Finnish lettu
items.flavor: Thin Finnish pancakes, served with jam, sugar, or whipped cream.

items.name: Flemish pannekoeken
items.flavor: Thick Flemish pancakes, finished with brown sugar and butter.

items.name: Flensjes
items.flavor: Paper-thin Frisian crepes, stacked or rolled with sugar.

items.name: Flija
items.flavor: A layered Albanian batter dish, baked in many thin sheets until the top is golden.

items.name: Florida plantain pancakes
items.flavor: Sweet ripe plantain, a little cinnamon, and a fried edge.

items.name: Flour tortillas
items.flavor: Soft, wheaty, and a little rich from fat, with browned spots and a flexible crumb.

items.name: Frixuelos
items.flavor: Asturian Carnival pancakes, a little richer than Galician filloas, with lemon.

items.name: Galette complète
items.flavor: A buckwheat galette with ham, cheese, and an egg cooked in the middle.

items.name: Galette-saucisse
items.flavor: A pork sausage rolled in a buckwheat galette, the Rennes street snack.

items.name: Gamjajeon
items.flavor: A pan-fried potato cake, crisp at the lace and soft inside, with scallion and sesame.

items.name: Gaziantep katmer
items.flavor: Crisp layered flatbread filled with pistachio and kaymak, which is clotted cream.

items.name: Georgia peach pancakes
items.flavor: Juicy ripe peach against a tangy buttermilk crumb, sweet but not candied.

items.name: Georgian mchadi
items.flavor: Dense cornmeal cakes with a toasted crust and a mildly sweet grain center.

items.name: German Eierkuchen
items.flavor: Thin German egg pancakes. In Berlin, do not call them Pfannkuchen.

items.name: Ghanaian tatale
items.flavor: Sweet ripe plantain fritters with ginger and a mild chile warmth, fried until the edges crisp.

items.name: Gingerbread pancakes
items.flavor: Dark molasses, ginger, cinnamon, and clove in a soft wheat cake.

items.name: Goan alebele
items.flavor: A thin, tender crepe rolled around fresh coconut and jaggery, with cardamom in the filling.

items.name: Gorditas
items.flavor: Thick toasted masa, split and filled with mashed beans, fresh cheese, and a mild salsa.

items.name: Greek tiganites
items.flavor: Small Greek fried pancakes finished with honey and cinnamon.

items.name: Haemul pajeon
items.flavor: A crisp scallion pancake threaded with shrimp and squid, mild chile in the dip.

items.name: Haitian accras
items.flavor: Fried grated malanga, herb-heavy and crisp, with a soft center that has to be cooked through.

items.name: Hawaiian banana-macadamia hotcakes
items.flavor: Ripe banana and toasted macadamia in a rich diner hotcake.

items.name: Hiroshima okonomiyaki
items.flavor: A layered savory crepe: thin batter, a mound of cabbage, noodles, pork, and egg, finished with sauce.

items.name: Honduran baleadas
items.flavor: A soft griddled wheat tortilla folded over refried beans and crumbled cheese.

items.name: Hopi piki
items.flavor: Very thin toasted blue corn, delicate and dry enough to fold, with a mineral note if ash is used.

items.name: Hortobágyi palacsinta
items.flavor: Hungarian crepes filled with paprika chicken, folded, and baked with sour cream.

items.name: Hotteok
items.flavor: A chewy street pancake split by molten brown sugar, cinnamon, and walnut.

items.name: Hudson Valley buckwheat cakes
items.flavor: Sour, earthy buckwheat with a molasses edge and a crisp griddle face.

items.name: Hungarian palacsinta
items.flavor: Thin Hungarian crepes rolled with apricot jam.

items.name: Icelandic lummur
items.flavor: Small thick Icelandic pancakes with rye, buttered and sugared.

items.name: Icelandic pönnukökur
items.flavor: Very thin Icelandic pancakes, rolled with sugar or rhubarb jam.

items.name: Imagawayaki
items.flavor: A round filled cake cooked in a hinged iron, with sweet red bean paste sealed inside a soft wheat shell.

items.name: Indian slapjack
items.flavor: Soft corn, milk, and egg, with only a little wheat to hold the cake.

items.name: Injera
items.flavor: Sour, spongy teff bread with an earthy crumb and open holes on top.

items.name: Irish boxty
items.flavor: Pan boxty: raw grated potato and mashed potato, fried as cakes.

items.name: Irish oatmeal pancakes
items.flavor: Soft oatmeal pancakes with buttermilk, a breakfast cake from Irish kitchens.

items.name: Irish potato farls
items.flavor: Mashed-potato farls, cut in quarters and cooked on a griddle.

items.name: Jamaican bammy
items.flavor: A dense, mild cassava round, dry and toasted on the outside, then fried so the edge crisps.

items.name: Jamaican festival
items.flavor: Sweet cornmeal and wheat dumplings, fried until deep gold, with a soft center.

items.name: Japanese hotcakes
items.flavor: Thick, soft cafe hotcakes with a browned top, butter, and syrup, taller than a thin crepe and gentler than a souffle cake.

items.name: Jingalov hats
items.flavor: A thin griddled flatbread packed with a large handful of salted herbs and greens.

items.name: Jowar dosa
items.flavor: A pale sorghum dosa, mildly sweet and peppery, with a dry crisp edge.

items.name: Kaiserschmarrn
items.flavor: A torn, caramelized Austrian pancake with raisins and plum compote.

items.name: Kartoffelpuffer
items.flavor: Shredded German potato pancakes, crisp, with applesauce.

items.name: Kenyan chapati
items.flavor: Soft, flaky wheat flatbread with a lightly oiled, toasted surface.

items.name: Kenyan vitumbua
items.flavor: Yeasted rice cakes scented with coconut and cardamom, crisp on the curve and soft inside.

items.name: Khanom bueang
items.flavor: A crisp rice crepe folded around a sweet coconut-egg topping, lacy at the edge.

items.name: Khanom krok
items.flavor: Small coconut-rice cakes with a browned rim and a soft, sweet center, cooked in a dimpled pan.

items.name: Kimchi jeon
items.flavor: A tangy, medium-hot pancake of ripe kimchi in a wheat batter, crisp at the edge.

items.name: Kolbullar
items.flavor: A simple pork and flour pancake from the charcoal woods of central Sweden.

items.name: Kue ape
items.flavor: A small coconut-rice cake with a crisp rim and a soft center that sinks into a crater.

items.name: Kuku sabzi
items.flavor: A dense herb frittata, bright green inside, with walnut and a sour note from barberries.

items.name: Kuzhi paniyaram
items.flavor: Small fermented rice-and-urad balls, crisp outside, soft inside, with mustard seed and curry leaf.

items.name: Lacy cornbread
items.flavor: Crisp, salty corn with a brittle lace of holes and a tender spot in the middle.

items.name: Lancashire potato cakes
items.flavor: Thick mashed-potato cakes, fried, from Lancashire breakfasts.

items.name: Latvian potato pancakes
items.flavor: Latvian pancakes of half mashed and half raw potato, with dill, fried in butter.

items.name: Lebanese manakish
items.flavor: Soft round flatbread topped with thyme, sumac, sesame, and olive oil.

items.name: Lemon ricotta pancakes
items.flavor: Soft, custardy ricotta cakes with bright lemon zest and a light crumb.

items.name: Lithuanian bulviniai blynai
items.flavor: Lithuanian potato pancakes with kefir in the batter, fried and served with sour cream.

items.name: Llapingachos
items.flavor: Pan-fried potato cakes with cheese inside and a mild peanut sauce over the top.

items.name: Lowcountry rice griddle cakes
items.flavor: Soft, lightly sweet rice cakes with a crisp buttered edge and separate grains in the crumb.

items.name: Maine blueberry pancakes
items.flavor: Tart wild blueberries bursting into a buttered, lightly sweet wheat cake.

items.name: Malawach
items.flavor: Flaky laminated flatbread, salty and toasted, with a pull-apart layer at the edge.

items.name: Malpua
items.flavor: A fried sweet pancake, fennel-scented, soaked in sugar syrup until the edges lacquer.

items.name: Mandarin pancakes
items.flavor: Very thin wheat pancakes, soft and faintly sesame-scented, made to wrap crisp duck skin and meat.

items.name: Markook saj bread
items.flavor: Paper-thin wheat flatbread, soft and lightly smoky from a few seconds on a dome.

items.name: Martabak manis
items.flavor: A thick, sweet pancake, also called terang bulan, topped with chocolate, cheese, and peanuts.

items.name: Martabak telur
items.flavor: A thin, crisp wheat skin folded around a juicy filling of egg, seasoned beef, and onion.

items.name: Martinican accras de morue
items.flavor: Salt-cod fritters in a wheat batter, garlicky and medium-hot, fried until the crust shatters.

items.name: Masala dosa
items.flavor: A fermented rice-and-urad sheet wrapped around a turmeric potato filling, with curry leaf and green chile.

items.name: Matzo brei
items.flavor: Soft scrambled egg bound around soaked matzo, salty and toasted in butter.

items.name: Mauritian crepes
items.flavor: Thin French Creole crepes with a vanilla batter, folded over brown sugar.

items.name: Memiljeon
items.flavor: A nutty buckwheat pancake, earthy and a little bitter, bound with egg and scallion.

items.name: Mexican buñuelos
items.flavor: Thin, crisp fried dough with anise, broken into shards and soaked with piloncillo and cinnamon syrup.

items.name: Mexican hotcakes
items.flavor: Soft wheat cakes with browned butter, finished with cajeta, honey, or condensed milk.

items.name: Michigan cherry pancakes
items.flavor: Tart cherry against a lightly sweet buttermilk cake.

items.name: Minnesota wild rice pancakes
items.flavor: A wheat pancake with chewy, toasted grains of wild rice scattered through it.

items.name: Mofo gasy
items.flavor: Small, sweet rice cakes with a yeasted crumb and a browned top.

items.name: Molasses pancakes
items.flavor: Strong, dark molasses in a tender wheat crumb, bittersweet rather than floral.

items.name: Monjayaki
items.flavor: A loose, runny savory batter cooked on a griddle and eaten while it is still half set.

items.name: Mont lin maya
items.flavor: A pair of small rice cakes from a dimpled pan, one plain and one topped with split peas and shallot, joined together.

items.name: Moong dal cheela
items.flavor: A soft yellow-lentil pancake, bright with ginger and green chile, less nutty than a besan cheela.

items.name: Moroccan baghrir
items.flavor: Spongy semolina cakes, yeasted and sour-sweet, soaked with butter and honey.

items.name: Moroccan harcha
items.flavor: Crumbly semolina pan bread, buttery and lightly salty, with a toasted crust.

items.name: Msemen
items.flavor: Flaky, lightly salty layered flatbread with toasted semolina between the folds.

items.name: Mysore masala dosa
items.flavor: A crisp fermented dosa spread inside with red chile-garlic chutney and a line of potato masala.

items.name: Nalysnyky
items.flavor: Ukrainian crepes rolled with cheese and baked in sour cream.

items.name: Navajo frybread
items.flavor: Fried wheat dough, blistered and salty, crisp outside and soft inside.

items.name: Neer dosa
items.flavor: A soft, pale, almost translucent rice roll with a clean cereal taste and no sour ferment.

items.name: Negiyaki
items.flavor: A scallion-heavy savory pancake, sweeter and greener than cabbage okonomiyaki, with a soft wheat crumb.

items.name: Nei appam
items.flavor: A sweet, dense rice cake scented with banana, jaggery, cardamom, and ghee.

items.name: New England cornmeal cakes
items.flavor: Coarse corn and molasses against a tangy buttermilk crumb.

items.name: New Mexico blue corn hotcakes
items.flavor: Toasted blue corn in a tender buttermilk cake, nutty and a little sweet.

items.name: New Orleans calas
items.flavor: Fried rice fritters, lightly sweet, with nutmeg and a powdered-sugar coat.

items.name: New Zealand pikelets
items.flavor: Small tea-table pikelets with a golden edge, finished with butter and golden syrup.

items.name: Newfoundland toutons
items.flavor: Fried bread dough, crisp at the rim, with salt pork and a side of molasses.

items.name: Nicaraguan güirilas
items.flavor: Thick young-corn pancakes with cuajada folded in, savory and a little milky, barely sweet.

items.name: Nigerian masa
items.flavor: Mildly sour rice cakes with crisp rims and a soft, slightly sweet center.

items.name: Normandy apple crepes
items.flavor: Wheat crepes filled with apples cooked in butter, a Normandy dessert.

items.name: Norwegian lefse
items.flavor: Potato lefse, rolled thin and griddled, soft enough to fold with butter and sugar.

items.name: Oaxacan memelas
items.flavor: An elongated masa cake spread with oil, black beans, and a mild salsa, toasted at the edges.

items.name: Oladyi
items.flavor: Small thick Russian pancakes on kefir, quicker than yeasted blini.

items.name: Onion rava dosa
items.flavor: Crisp semolina lace crowded with sweet onion, green chile, and curry leaf.

items.name: Osaka okonomiyaki
items.flavor: A thick savory pancake with cabbage mixed into the batter, topped with sauce, mayonnaise, and bonito flakes.

items.name: Pajeon
items.flavor: A savory wheat pancake packed with scallion, crisp at the rim and tender in the middle.

items.name: Palak cheela
items.flavor: A green spinach and gram-flour pancake, savory with ginger and cumin, soft rather than crisp.

items.name: Paper dosa
items.flavor: A very large, very thin fermented rice sheet that shatters at the edge and tastes toasted.

items.name: Paraguayan mbeju
items.flavor: A crisp griddled cake of manioc starch, cornmeal, and cheese, salty at the edge and tender in the middle.

items.name: Parāoa parai
items.flavor: Fried wheat bread, puffed and crisp at the rim, with a soft, salty interior.

items.name: Patishapta
items.flavor: A soft rice-and-wheat crepe rolled around a coconut and jaggery filling, fragrant with cardamom.

items.name: Pennsylvania Dutch funnel cakes
items.flavor: Crisp fried batter, lightly eggy, buried under powdered sugar.

items.name: Pennsylvania Dutch potato pancakes
items.flavor: Shredded potato, onion, and pepper, crisp at the edge and soft in the middle.

items.name: Peruvian tacu-tacu
items.flavor: A pan-fried cake of leftover rice and beans, garlicky, with a crisp face and mild ají amarillo.

items.name: Pesarattu
items.flavor: A green-gold moong dal pancake, herbal from ginger and green chile, with a soft crisp edge.

items.name: Piadina
items.flavor: The griddled flatbread of Romagna. It is a flatbread, folded around a filling.

items.name: Placki ziemniaczane
items.flavor: Polish potato pancakes, shredded and fried, with sugar or sour cream.

items.name: Plain dosa
items.flavor: Crisp at the edge, faintly sour, with a toasted rice smell and a soft underside.

items.name: Poffertjes
items.flavor: Small yeast pancakes from a dimpled Dutch pan, buttered and dusted with sugar.

items.name: Pol roti
items.flavor: A griddled coconut flatbread, lightly sweet from the coconut, with onion and green chile in the dough.

items.name: Polish naleśniki
items.flavor: Thin Polish crepes with a sweet cheese filling, rolled and warmed.

items.name: Portuguese panquecas
items.flavor: Thin Portuguese crepes with orange zest, rolled with jam.

items.name: Portuguese rabanadas
items.flavor: Portuguese Christmas fried bread, soaked in milk and egg, with cinnamon sugar. Not a poured pancake.

items.name: Potato latkes
items.flavor: Ashkenazi potato pancakes for Hanukkah, fried in oil, with the older cheese custom named beside them.

items.name: Pudla

journeys.title: Who settled the flavor
journeys.dek: A rail route across the United States, tasting the cakes settlers, immigrants, and older corn traditions left on the griddle.
intro: This train does not hand the country to one kitchen. It stops where a cake can be tied to a real migration, a crop, or a dispute about the name.
Read the essay first if you want the argument in one place. The pancakes are the evidence.

journeys.title: Crepes by balloon
journeys.dek: A low, slow pass over Brittany and the north of France, from wheat crepes to buckwheat galettes.
intro: A balloon is the right speed for this coast. The batter changes faster than the landscape: white flour and milk, then buckwheat, ham, and egg.
Chandeleur, not Mardi Gras, is the French crepe day. The pages say so.

journeys.title: Butter week by plane
journeys.dek: Shrove Tuesday, Candlemas, and Maslenitsa. The plane is honest about the distance between these fast days.
intro: These are not the same holiday. England clears the pantry on Shrove Tuesday. France makes crepes at Chandeleur. Russia spends a week on blini before Lent.
The plane hops the calendar as well as the map. Each page names its own day.

journeys.title: Dosas by train

journeys.title: East Asia's savory cakes by plane
journeys.dek: Jianbing, scallion pancake, okonomiyaki, and jeon. A flight, because these cities are not a day's walk apart.
intro: Osaka and Hiroshima do not make the same okonomiyaki. Tianjin jianbing is not a Shandong jianbing. The plane stops treat them as neighbors, not as one dish with a new sauce.
This is a savory route. Dorayaki and sweet hotteok are in the journal, on another page.

journeys.title: Africa coast to coast
journeys.dek: From a Moroccan baghrir to a South African pannekoek, with fermented batters in between.
intro: The coasts are not one cuisine. Baghrir, masa, injera, canjeero, and pannekoek do not descend from each other. The plane is only a way to taste them in one reading.
Where a cake is tied to a trade in grain, the page says which grain.

The route starts in Mexico and ends with a Brazilian tapioca crepe, which is not masa at all. That last hop is a reminder that the map of griddled cakes does not stop at corn.

journeys.title: The potato road by train

books.dek: Buckwheat, sorghum, dried apple, and corn on an upland griddle.
intro: These are the cakes that can be tied to the upland South: buckwheat, sorghum, dried apple, molasses, and a cornmeal griddle.

Scots-Irish and English settlers brought oat and wheat habits into the mountains. Corn was already there. Enslaved people and later Black Appalachian cooks worked the same kitchens. This book does not treat the mountains as one family's pantry.

books.title: Shrove Tuesday Around the World
books.dek: The late-winter custom of using eggs and fat, with each feast day named honestly.
intro: Shrove Tuesday is the English and Irish day. It is not the name of every pancake holiday.

French crepes on this route belong to Chandeleur, 2 February. Russian blini belong to Maslenitsa, butter week. Galician filloas belong to Carnival. The pages say which day is which. The book is a route through that season, not a claim that the whole world keeps an English Tuesday.

passages.title: Appalachian Griddle Cakes
passages.text: Scots-Irish and English settlers brought oat and wheat habits into the mountains. Corn was already there. Enslaved people and later Black Appalachian cooks worked the same kitchens. This book does not treat the mountains as one family's pantry.
passages.label: From the book

passages.title: Australian pikelets
passages.text: Australian pikelets are small thick pancakes dropped by the spoon, a British inheritance on the tea table. Drop scones and pikelets traveled with British settlers and stayed as afternoon-tea food, the kind made for a visit or a church hall. They are not the large thin pancake. That cake has its own page, with a looser batter, a wider pan, and lemon and sugar. Pikelets are the small ones, buttered and jammed.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Australian pancakes
passages.text: These are the larger Australian pancakes, thinner than pikelets and finished with lemon and sugar. British settlers brought that lemon-and-sugar habit, and weekend pans still use it. The batter on this page is looser than a pikelet batter, and the cakes are cooked wider in the pan. Pikelets remain the small thick tea cakes. They are a different recipe, with less milk and a smaller spoon, and they are not repeated here.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: New Zealand pikelets
passages.text: New Zealand pikelets come from the same British drop-scone cooking that settlers carried south. On this tea table they are a batch for morning or afternoon tea, the small thick cakes home cooks still stir up without a special occasion. The pin is Dunedin, a city with a strong Scottish settlement history, and the cakes are not a Dunedin invention. They are a national home recipe. Golden syrup and butter finish this batch. The Australian pikelet page is a different write-up, with jam, and it is not copied here.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Parāoa parai
passages.text: Parāoa parai is Māori fried bread. Parāoa is the word for flour and for bread, and parai means fried. Wheat flour reached Māori kitchens through trade and the colonial economy, including the long pressure on Māori land. This is not a pre-contact food. It is a fried dough that became ordinary kai, cooked at home and for gatherings. The pin is Whanganui. The bread is cooked in Māori homes well beyond that river. This recipe fries a simple baking-powder dough.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Mauritian crepes
passages.text: Mauritian crepes are the thin pancakes of French Creole cooking on the island, made at home and sold on the street in Port Louis and at fairs. French colonial kitchens left the crepe. Mauritian cooks kept it beside a table that is also Indian, African, and Chinese. This page is only the crepe: a thin wheat batter with vanilla, cooked in a small pan and folded with brown sugar. It is not a Breton galette and not a dholl puri. Mauritius is filed under East Africa on this map.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Filipino hotcakes
passages.text: Filipino hotcakes are a 20th century breakfast. American colonial influence brought wheat pancakes and canned milk into Philippine kitchens, and the cakes stayed after that period as a local morning food. Homes and small cafes cook them in margarine and serve them with sugar or sweetened condensed milk more often than with maple syrup. They sit beside rice meals. They did not replace rice. This page tells that history directly. The batter is wheat, egg, and milk, a modern breakfast cake, not a precolonial rice cake.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Dominican casabe
passages.text: Casabe comes from Taíno cooking on the island. People in the Dominican Republic still make it and buy it. What you find in a shop today is a processed flatbread: cassava that has already been turned into flour or into packaged rounds, then cooked until dry. This recipe uses commercial cassava flour. It does not reconstruct a pre-colonial kitchen, and it does not teach you to process raw bitter cassava at home. Wheat breads arrived later. Casabe is the older starch on this table.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Peruvian tacu-tacu
passages.text: Tacu-tacu is a cake of leftover rice and beans, fried in a skillet until the outside is crisp. It is Lima criollo cooking. Afro-Peruvian cooks helped build that coastal cuisine in the colonial city and afterward, working with Indigenous ingredients and Spanish techniques in kitchens shaped by slavery and, later, by free Black communities. The dish itself is practical: the previous day's rice and beans, garlic, onion, and ají amarillo, pressed into a hot pan. A fried egg or a breaded steak is a common addition. Those are not in this recipe.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Appalachian buckwheat cakes
passages.text: Appalachian buckwheat cakes use flour milled from buckwheat, a crop that grows on cooler mountain ground, usually mixed with wheat flour so the cake holds together. Scots-Irish and English settlement lines up with this griddle, and German-speaking neighbors lived in the same hills. Enslaved people and later Black Appalachian cooks worked many of the same farms. The cakes are a tangy breakfast, often finished with sorghum rather than maple.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Lowcountry rice griddle cakes
passages.text: Lowcountry rice griddle cakes use the long-grain rice of the South Carolina and Georgia coast. Enslaved West Africans brought rice-growing knowledge, and planters built a brutal rice economy on their labor and on the labor of their descendants. The cake is a later griddle use of that grain. It is not a rename of one village dish.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Sweet potato pancakes
passages.text: Sweet potato pancakes mash an orange-fleshed sweet potato into a wheat batter. Sweet potatoes have been a Southern field crop for a long time, in Native gardens and later in the kitchens of enslaved and free Black cooks and of white farm families. The griddle cake is a breakfast use of the mashed root. Wilson, North Carolina, is a modern market town for the crop and the map pin, not a claim that the pancake was invented there.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Hudson Valley buckwheat cakes
passages.text: Dutch settlers in the Hudson Valley cooked buckwheat cakes, and the grain fits a cool climate and a short season. The same grain shows up in other cold regions for that reason. Nineteenth-century New York breakfasts often included a yeasted buckwheat batter mixed with some wheat flour. These cakes are that Dutch-American breakfast, pinned at Kingston.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Pennsylvania Dutch funnel cakes
passages.text: Pennsylvania Dutch funnel cakes are batter fried in hot fat after it is poured through a funnel in looping strands. The name Pennsylvania Dutch means Deutsch, the German-speaking settlers of the region, not the Netherlands. Fair stands later carried the fried batter well beyond Lancaster County. Kutztown is the map pin.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Gingerbread pancakes
passages.text: Gingerbread pancakes are a seasonal American breakfast that borrows molasses, ginger, and cinnamon from gingerbread. They are a twentieth-century table idea, a spiced wheat cake for cold mornings. Philadelphia is the map pin because molasses moved through that port, not because a single colonial manuscript holds this pancake. The crumb is darker and sharper than a plain buttermilk pancake.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: Florida plantain pancakes
passages.text: These plantain pancakes are Cuban-American home cooking in Miami, where ripe plantains are mashed, bound with egg and a little flour, and fried in small cakes. The dish belongs to twentieth-century Cuban kitchens in the city. It is not a colonial-era recipe.
passages.label: From the field guide

passages.title: New Orleans calas
passages.text: New Orleans calas are fried rice fritters sold for generations by Black vendors, many of them women, who carried the cakes through the streets. Rice growing in Louisiana depended on the skill of enslaved West Africans and on the plantation economy built on their labor. This page does not claim that one West African village recipe became calas. The fritter that can be documented is the Creole rice cake sold in the city.
passages.label: From the field guide
